translationRepairs: In the seventh month Cao Prefecture fell to him.
In the seventh month Chanzhou fell to him.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Cao Prefecture would be 曹州.
In the seventh month he took Cao Prefecture.
In the seventh month he took Chanzhou.
The literal field repeats the same mistaken identification of 澶州 as Cao Prefecture.
In the eighth month Liang recovered Cao. Jin and Liu Yan faced off at Xin; Jin taunted him day after day, but Yan barred his gates and would not fight.
In the eighth month Liang recovered Chanzhou. Jin and Liu Yan faced off at Xin; Jin taunted him day after day, but Yan barred his gates and would not fight.
梁復取澶州 says Liang recovered Chanzhou, not Cao Prefecture.
In the eighth month Liang retook Cao Prefecture. The Jin and Yan armies faced each other at Xin; the Jin army repeatedly challenged battle, but Yan shut his walls and would not come out.
In the eighth month Liang retook Chanzhou. The Jin and Yan armies faced each other at Xin; the Jin army repeatedly challenged battle, but Yan shut his walls and would not come out.
The literal field also confuses 澶州 with 曹州; Chanzhou is correct.
In the eleventh year, the Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang was killed at Taiyuan, and his father Rengong was used at Yanmen.
In the eleventh year, the Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang was killed at Taiyuan, and his father Rengong was offered in sacrifice at Yanmen.
In this execution context 用 means that Liu Rengong was offered as a sacrifice at Yanmen, as the accompanying historical note confirms.
Khitan horsemen raided Weizhou and captured Li Siben, military governor of Zhenwu.
Khitan horsemen raided Yuzhou and captured Li Siben, military governor of Zhenwu.
蔚州 is Yuzhou; Weizhou represents a different place name.
The Khitan raided Weizhou and seized Zhenwu military governor Li Siben.
The Khitan raided Yuzhou and seized Zhenwu military governor Li Siben.
The literal field makes the same place-name error: 蔚州 is Yuzhou.
In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei monk named Zhenzhen offered up a Tang “Mandate of Heaven” seal.
In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei monk named Chuanzhen offered up a Tang “Mandate of Heaven” seal.
The monk is named 傳真, Chuanzhen; Zhenzhen drops the first character.
In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei prefectural monk, Zhenzhen, presented one Tang Mandate of Heaven treasure.
In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei prefectural monk, Chuanzhen, presented one Tang Mandate of Heaven treasure.
The literal field also mistransliterates 傳真, whose name is Chuanzhen.
Guo Chongtao, commissioner of the inner gate, and Zhang Juhun, Zhaoyi supervisor, were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Guo Chongtao, commissioner of the inner gate, and Zhang Juhan, Zhaoyi supervisor, were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
張居翰 is Zhang Juhan, consistent with his biography elsewhere in this book.
The inner-gate commissioner Guo Chongtao and the Zhaoyi army supervisory commissioner Zhang Juhun became commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
The inner-gate commissioner Guo Chongtao and the Zhaoyi army supervisory commissioner Zhang Juhan became commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
The literal field repeats the mistransliteration of 張居翰 as Zhang Juhun.
On guimao, Lady Liu was made empress.
On guiwei, Lady Liu was made empress.
癸未 is guiwei; guimao would represent 癸卯.
On the guimao day, Lady Liu was installed as empress.
On the guiwei day, Lady Liu was installed as empress.
The literal field makes the same sexagenary-day error: 癸未 is guiwei.
On xinsi, Li Jiyao was put to death.
On xinsi, Li Jitao was put to death.
李繼韜 is Li Jitao; 韜 is tao, not yao.
On the xinsi day, Li Jiyao was executed.
On the xinsi day, Li Jitao was executed.
The literal field repeats the mistransliteration of 李繼韜 as Li Jiyao.
On yimao, Dayu Mo arrived as envoy from the Parhae king.
On yimao, Dayu Mo arrived as envoy from the Parhae king Da Yinzhuan.
The source explicitly names the Balhae king 大諲譔, rendered Da Yinzhuan consistently elsewhere in this book.
On the yimao day, the Parhae king Geum’s envoy Dayu Mo came.
On the yimao day, the Parhae king Da Yinzhuan’s envoy Dayu Mo came.
The source names Da Yinzhuan; 'Geum' has no basis in 大諲譔.
On xinsi, Hunjie Lou of the Turks and the Parhae king each sent envoys.
On xinsi, Hunjie Lou of the Turks and the Parhae king Da Yinzhuan each sent envoys.
The source explicitly names the Balhae king 大諲撰; omitting him loses a named individual.
On the xinsi day, the Turk Hunjie Lou and the Parhae king both sent envoys.
On the xinsi day, the Turk Hunjie Lou and the Parhae king Da Yinzhuan both sent envoys.
The literal field also omits the explicitly named Balhae king Da Yinzhuan.
On guimao of the eighth month, Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, was executed.
On guiwei of the eighth month, Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, was executed.
癸未 is guiwei, not guimao.
On the guimao day of the eighth month, Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, was killed.
On the guiwei day of the eighth month, Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, was killed.
The literal field repeats the same sexagenary-day error for 癸未.
On guimao, he returned from White Sands.
On guiwei, he returned from White Sands.
癸未 is guiwei, not guimao.
On the guimao day, he returned from White Sands.
On the guiwei day, he returned from White Sands.
The literal field repeats the same sexagenary-day error for 癸未.

On xinhai of the intercalary month he enfeoffed his brothers: Cunmei as Prince of Yong, Cunba as Prince of Yong, Cunli as Prince of Xue, Cunwo as Prince of Shen, Cunyi as Prince of Mu, Cunque as Prince of Tong, and Cunji as Prince of Ya.

On xinhai of the intercalary month he enfeoffed his brothers: Cunmei as Prince of Yōng, Cunba as Prince of Yǒng, Cunli as Prince of Xue, Cunwo as Prince of Shen, Cunyi as Prince of Mu, Cunque as Prince of Tong, and Cunji as Prince of Ya.
邕王 and 永王 are distinct titles. Tone-marked Yōng and Yǒng preserve the distinction without inserting Chinese characters into an English field.
